name: L-citrulline

track.title: Phase III
track.line: None found; one tadalafil comparison recruiting

track.title: Dietary supplement
track.line: Sold as an amino acid; FDA does not review first

what.text: L-citrulline is an amino acid. The body converts it into L-arginine, which is used to make nitric oxide, a messenger that relaxes blood vessels. Researchers study it because, taken by mouth, it raises arginine levels without being broken down as much in the gut and liver as arginine itself.

what.text: There is little research on L-citrulline for erectile dysfunction: one small study of citrulline alone and one of citrulline combined with resveratrol.

research.text: Two small human studies were found. One gave L-citrulline alone to 24 men with mild ED for one month, without a full placebo control group. The other gave it with resveratrol to 20 men already using PDE5 drugs. The rest of the evidence is in rats. A trial comparing L-citrulline with tadalafil began recruiting in Egypt in 2026.

research.title: Men with mild ED, 2011

facts.v: single-blind: one month of placebo, then one month of L-citrulline (not randomized)
24 men with mild ED, mean age 56.5
2 months; 1.5 g a day in the citrulline month
erection hardness score, number of times having sex, satisfaction, side effects

research.found: Erection hardness rose from mild ED to normal in 2 of 24 men on placebo and 12 of 24 on L-citrulline. Sex rose from about 1.4 to 2.3 times a month. No side effects were reported. The authors wrote that it was less effective than PDE5 drugs.

src.label: Cormio L, et al. Urology 2011

research.title: With resveratrol in men already on PDE5 drugs, 2018

facts.v: 20 men with ED despite PDE5 drugs; 13 completed
one month each; L-citrulline 800 mg and resveratrol 300 mg a day, with their usual PDE5 drug
erectile function score (SHIM), erection hardness, ageing-male sexual score

research.found: The SHIM score was higher on the combination than on placebo. Erection hardness and the ageing-male score did not change significantly. Because citrulline was combined with resveratrol, the study cannot show the effect of citrulline alone.

research.title: L-citrulline vs tadalafil vs both (registered)

facts.v: 133 men with mild to moderate ED planned
12 weeks; L-citrulline 1,500 mg a day, tadalafil 5 mg, or both

research.found: Recruiting since June 2026. No results posted.

research.text: In rats with blocked pelvic arteries, L-citrulline in drinking water for 3 weeks improved erection pressure during nerve stimulation. These results have not been confirmed in people.

us.text: L-citrulline is not an FDA-approved drug for any use. It can be sold as a dietary supplement, which FDA does not approve or review for safety or effectiveness before sale. FDA is evaluating it as a substance for compounding. As of November 1, 2026.

side.text: The two small human studies reported no side effects, but they were short and tiny. As a supplement, L-citrulline is not reviewed by FDA for safety before sale.
